scope.core.proved: PROVED -- symbolic and universal under the hypotheses

scope.bisect.proved: THRESHOLD BRACKETED by a proof and a refutation
note.synth.proved:
THIS IS NOT A UNIVERSAL PROOF: the candidate holds in the
  domain above and nowhere else. For the general statement, run
  `certo synth --prove-candidate` or write a symbolic Spec with these
  values fixed and pass it to `certo prove`.
note.sweep.proved: The enumerated family for that n was checked, not every n.
cli.certificate.none: certificate: NONE -- nothing to audit here
cli.solution.more: ... {n} more (the full solution is in the certificate)
cli.starting_from: starting from the first counterexample of the sweep: {g6}
cli.no_counterexample: no counterexample to minimise: the sweep found none (examined: {n})
cli.universal.fail.detail: the candidate holds in the bounded domain but NOT in general
cli.universal.unavailable: UNIVERSAL PROOF: could not be built
engine.prove.refuted: REFUTED: there is a counterexample that satisfies the hypotheses and violates the claim
engine.check.unsat: no model exists; the core explains why
engine.synth.found: no counterexample left IN THE BOUNDED DOMAIN ({rounds} rounds, {ces} counterexamples)
engine.synth.none: no object satisfies the specification (refuted after {ces} counterexamples)
engine.synth.impl_unknown: the implementation solver did not conclude: {reason}
engine.synth.ce_unknown: the counterexample solver did not conclude: {reason}
engine.synth.no_universal: the spec does not define the universal obligation. Add to SynthSpec either `universal_behavior=<expr>` (simple case) or `universal=lambda vals: Spec(...)` (full control: lets you change sort and name the hypotheses)
engine.opt.exact_ilp: integer optimum found; the EXACT dual certifies the relaxation bound: {value}
engine.opt.float: optimum with a floating-point dual certificate
engine.opt.float.why: (no rational reconstruction verified; the certificate stays in floating point and is NOT citable)
engine.opt.negative_bound: variable {var}: negative lower bound. The standard dual certificate requires x >= 0; reformulate with non-negative variables.
engine.cases.sat: a case satisfying every constraint EXISTS
engine.cases.noproof: UNSATISFIABLE, but with no proof: nothing to audit. {detail}
engine.cases.badproof: the solver said UNSAT but the proof does NOT verify: {detail}
engine.enum.summary: {count} graphs on n={n} up to isomorphism{filtered}
engine.sweep.refuted.note: ({n} not evaluated, which does not affect the refutation)
engine.sweep.partial: no counterexample among the {examined} evaluated, but {n} were NOT EVALUATED: it cannot be claimed to hold across the family
engine.sweep.proved: the predicate holds on all {count} graphs with n={n} (FINITE CASE, not the theorem)
engine.shrink.not_ce: the starting graph is NOT a counterexample: {why}
engine.shrink.minimal: minimal counterexample: n={n} m={m} (from n={n0} m={m0}, {steps} reductions)
engine.mus.not_unsat: the starting formula is not unsatisfiable ({status}): there is no MUS to extract
engine.mus.noproof: the MUS did not come back unsatisfiable with a proof
engine.bisect.bad_good: the 'good' endpoint t={t} does not hold ({status}): the interval or the direction is wrong
engine.bisect.bad_bad: the 'bad' endpoint t={t} does not fail ({status}): the threshold is outside the interval, or the direction is inverted
engine.bisect.summary: threshold at {where} (holds at t={good}, fails at t={bad}; {probes} probes)
engine.bisect.build_type: build(t) must return a Spec or a CNFSpec, it returned {type}
cert.note.model: Verified by substitution and simplification; no search required.
cert.note.unsat_core: Verifying requires re-solving, but only the core (far smaller).
cert.note.lp_dual.exact: Optimality certified in EXACT rationals: primal and dual feasibility plus c.x = b.y, all in Fraction. No tolerances and no trust in CBC.
cert.note.lp_dual.float: Weak duality in FLOATING POINT, with a tolerance. Fine for exploring; citing a constant needs exact mode.
cert.note.cegis: The list of counterexamples IS the certificate: it is the minimal set of inputs that pins this solution down.
cert.note.cnf_model: Checked clause by clause. No solver, no propagation.
cert.note.drat: Refutation proof. Checked by unit propagation (RUP/RAT): no SAT solver is involved, so the one that produced it need not be trusted.
cert.note.shrink_graph: Minimal (1-minimal), not minimum. `blocked` is the witness: every one-step reduction either fails a filter or satisfies the predicate. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.
cert.note.mus: Minimal unsatisfiable subset. The DRAT proof refutes the MUS and each witness is a model of the MUS without one of its clauses: together they certify unsatisfiability AND minimality without a solver.
cert.note.bisect: The threshold is certified by the pair that brackets it: a proof on the good side and a refutation on the bad side. Each is verified separately. MONOTONICITY in t is assumed, not proved.
cert.note.synth_proved: Two chained obligations: the bounded synthesis that found the candidate and the universal symbolic proof of it. Each is verified separately; the one that counts as a theorem is the second.
cert.note.sweep: Two different things: which family was examined (verifiable here) and whether the predicate was evaluated correctly on each graph (only if the predicate supplied a certificate: {certified} of {total} entries). COMPLETENESS of the family requires re-enumerating.
cert.note.graph_set: Verifies pairwise non-isomorphism and the filters. COMPLETENESS (that none is missing) can only be checked by re-enumerating.
verify.model.fails: the assignment does NOT satisfy the formula
verify.core.detail: core of {n} formulas (includes the negated claim)
verify.lp.exact.detail: EXACT rational arithmetic, no tolerances: optimum = {value}
verify.lp.float.detail: weak duality with a tolerance; to cite it, re-run in exact mode
verify.lp.float.warning: FLOATING-POINT certificate with tolerance 1e-6: not usable to cite an exact constant
verify.cegis.impl_ok: the implementation satisfies its own constraints
verify.drat.formula: the formula matches the declared one ({n} clauses)
verify.drat.steps: the proof is RUP/RAT step by step
verify.drat.detail: {steps} steps ({rup} RUP, {rat} RAT, {del} deletions) in {ms:.0f} ms
verify.sweep.stats: the statistics match the stored values
verify.sweep.detail: family of {n} graphs; does NOT verify completeness (that needs re-enumerating)
verify.sweep.missing: {missing} of {total} entries have NO certificate from the predicate: the sweep says which graphs were examined, not that the predicate was evaluated correctly. Return Outcome(ok, cert=...) from the predicate to close that.
verify.sweep.unevaluated: {n} graphs were never evaluated (errors or inconclusive)
verify.shrink.still_ce: the minimal graph is still a counterexample
verify.shrink.none_survive: no one-step reduction is still a counterexample
verify.mus.subset: the MUS clauses come from the original formula
verify.mus.proof: the DRAT proof refutes the MUS
verify.mus.minimal: every MUS clause is needed (witness model)
verify.mus.detail: unsatisfiability AND minimality, without a solver
verify.bisect.detail: monotonicity in t is ASSUMED, not verified
verify.synth.detail: candidate {candidate}: the half that counts as a theorem is the second
verify.provenance.gone: the spec that produced it is no longer at {path}
verify.provenance.changed: CAREFUL: {path} has changed since this certificate was issued. The certificate is still valid on its own, but it no longer corresponds to the file that is there now.
verify.provenance.legacy: certificate without provenance: issued by an earlier version, it cannot be tied to the spec that produced it
spec.no_function: {name} does not define a spec() function
engine.domain.proved: the predicate holds on all {count} items (FINITE DOMAIN, not the theorem)
cert.note.domain_sweep: An exhaustive sweep over a finite domain the SPEC defined. Verifiable here: the ids are unique, the statistics match the stored values, and each predicate certificate checks out. NOT verifiable here: that the domain is complete or that the ids denote what they claim -- that is the spec's responsibility.
verify.domain.detail: domain of {n} items; does NOT verify completeness -- the spec defines it
verify.family.programmable: {names} cannot be re-checked here: a programmable filter lives in the spec
cert.note.sweep_range: One sub-certificate per size, verified separately. What this adds is the ORDER and the claim that nothing failed below the first failure. With --stop-on-first the larger sizes were never run.
verify.range.ordered: the sizes are in increasing order
verify.range.nothing_below: nothing failed below the first failure
verify.range.stopped: stopped at the first failure: the larger sizes were NOT examined
cli.range.none: range n={lo}..{hi}: no counterexample at any size
cli.lean.unverified: checked against Lean/Mathlib v4.28.0; another version may need adjusting
engine.core.matrix: {goals} goals x {hyps} hypotheses; never used by any goal: {unused}
engine.core.matrix_none: none of the {n} goals could be proved: there is no table to build
cert.note.core_matrix: One unsat core per goal, each verified separately. What the table adds is the comparison: a hypothesis needed by one goal and not another tells you how small a downstream interface can be.
verify.matrix.agrees: the table agrees with the cores
verify.matrix.inconclusive: {n} goals could not be proved; their column is empty, not false
cli.matrix.legend: yes = the goal's core needs it | no = redundant for that goal | ? = goal not proved
engine.shrink.no_reduce: this DomainSpec has no `reduce`: shrink needs to know what 'one step smaller' means. Add reduce=lambda item: [...] returning the smaller items.
cert.note.shrink_domain: Minimal (1-minimal), not minimum. The trace records the index taken into reduce() at each step, so verification replays the exact descent instead of re-running the search. `blocked` is the witness that no one-step reduction survives. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.
verify.shrink.replay: the descent replays to the same item
verify.shrink.item_missing: the starting item is not in the spec's domain: {id}
cli.ledger.summary: {total} entries: {ok} verified, {failed} FAILED, {tampered} changed since logged, {missing} missing, {no_cert} without certificate, {corrupt} corrupt
engine.range.first: range n={lo}..{hi}: first failure at n={first}
engine.range.none: range n={lo}..{hi}: no counterexample at any size
verify.shrink.still_ce_item: the minimal item is still a counterexample
engine.farkas.found: {mode} certificate found: {n} hypotheses with a non-zero multiplier
engine.farkas.none: no {mode} certificate exists for this system
engine.farkas.not_polynomial: cannot be put in polynomial form: {detail}
engine.farkas.nonlinear_needed: the system is not linear. Re-run with --nonlinear (nonlinear=true over MCP), which is the nlinarith preprocessing, or use `prove`, which decides real arithmetic completely
engine.farkas.inexact: the multipliers could not be reconstructed as exact rationals, so there is nothing citable to emit
cert.note.farkas: Non-negative rational multipliers whose combination cancels every monomial and closes the system. Verified by multiplying and adding in Fraction: no solver, no search. This is what linarith emits; with nonlinear=true the extra rows are products and squares of the hypotheses, which is what nlinarith adds.
verify.farkas.closes: the remaining constant is a contradiction
verify.farkas.declared: the declared constant and strictness match
verify.farkas.derived: {n} rows are products or squares derived from the hypotheses, not hypotheses themselves
spec.duplicate_lemma: there is already a lemma called {name}
spec.lemma_no_source: lemma {name} needs either proves=<Spec> or certificate=<path>
spec.lemma_no_statement: lemma {name} comes from a stored certificate, so it must declare states=<formula>: nothing can guess what that certificate licenses
engine.compose.no_goal: the proof has no theorem; call conclude()
engine.compose.bad_via: lemma {name}: via={via} is not an engine (prove, farkas, nlinarith)
engine.compose.link_failed: lemma {name} was proved, but what its certificate establishes does not entail the statement being used downstream. That gap is exactly what compose exists to catch
engine.compose.cert_invalid: lemma {name}: its certificate does not verify ({detail})
engine.compose.step_failed: the lemmas do not close the theorem [{status}]: {detail}
engine.compose.proved: theorem assembled from {lemmas} lemmas ({derived} derived and linked, {bridges} asserted)
cert.note.proof: A proof assembled from lemmas. Each lemma carries its own certificate AND the link showing that what the certificate establishes entails the statement used downstream. Lemmas marked as bridges are verified but not linked: the step from what they establish to a formula is a modelling decision, and it is listed by name so the reader can weigh it.
verify.proof.link: lemma {name}: its certificate entails the statement used
verify.proof.step_link: the final step uses only the lemmas and the theorem's own hypotheses
verify.proof.unused: lemmas the theorem does not need: {names}
numerics.no_backend: rigorous numerics needs python-flint (preferred) or mpmath: pip install python-flint
numerics.float: {value} is a Python float, and a float is not the decimal it is written as (0.1 is really 3602879701896397/2^55). An enclosure built from it would be rigorous about the wrong number. Write it as a string or a Fraction
numerics.not_a_number: {value} is not something an enclosure can be built from (use int, Fraction or a string)
numerics.unsupported: {backend} has no rigorous {name}; install python-flint, which does
engine.bounds.no_value: the spec has no value= callable
engine.bounds.measured: the value lies in [{lo}, {hi}], enclosed rigorously at {prec} bits
engine.bounds.refuted: {claim} is FALSE: the whole enclosure [{lo}, {hi}] lies on the other side
engine.bounds.undecided: the enclosure [{lo}, {hi}] still straddles the bound at {prec} bits. This is not a refutation: raise max_prec, or tighten the expression where it cancels
cert.note.ball: A rigorous enclosure of a real quantity, as EXACT rationals, and the claim it settles. Whether the interval settles the claim is decided by comparing fractions, with no library involved. Reproducing the interval needs the spec and the same backend, and is checked separately.
verify.ball.no_claim: no claim: the enclosure is the result
verify.ball.reproduced: re-evaluating the spec lands inside it
verify.ball.no_spec: the interval settles the claim, but the spec is not here ({path}), so nothing re-derived it: this certificate is only half checked
verify.ball.not_redone: could not re-evaluate the spec ({reason}); the rational half was still checked
engine.prove.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses contradict each other, so this goal -- and every other goal -- follows. The proof is valid and says nothing. Run `check` on the hypotheses alone to find which pair clashes.
engine.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses close the system without the goal at all, so they are contradictory and any goal would have been proved.
verify.core.vacuous: VACUOUS: this core does not include the negated goal, so the hypotheses contradict each other and the proof holds for any goal.
verify.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses were found to close the system without the goal, so they are contradictory and any goal would follow. The certificate is valid and says nothing.
verify.proof.vacuous: VACUOUS: the lemmas contradict each other, so the theorem -- and any other -- follows from them. Check the lemma statements against each other before citing this.
cli.vacuous: the hypotheses are contradictory: this proof is vacuous
scope.sweep.certified: FINITE CASE CERTIFIED -- not the theorem
scope.sweep.reproducible: FINITE SWEEP REPRODUCIBLE -- the predicate is NOT certified
scope.sweep.recorded: FINITE SWEEP RECORDED -- the predicate is NOT certified
cli.sweep.level.reproducible: {n} of {total} evaluations carry no certificate. The sweep is REPRODUCIBLE -- re-running the predicate gives the same answers -- but nothing here establishes that those answers are right. Return an Outcome with cert= to certify them.
cli.sweep.level.recorded: {n} of {total} evaluations carry no certificate and no verdict vector was recorded, so this is a RECORD of a run, not a check of one. Only the domain and its hash can be verified.
verify.sweep.replay: re-running the predicate gives the same verdicts
verify.sweep.replay.domain_moved: the spec no longer enumerates the same domain
verify.sweep.replay.gone: the spec is no longer at the recorded path
verify.sweep.replay.changed: the spec has changed since the run
verify.sweep.replay.skipped: the predicate was NOT re-run ({reason}), so nothing here checks what it answered
verify.sweep.uncertified.reproducible: {n} of {total} evaluations carry no certificate. Replaying them agrees, which makes the sweep reproducible; it does NOT make the predicate's answers verified.
verify.sweep.uncertified.recorded: {n} of {total} evaluations carry no certificate and could not be replayed. Only the domain and its hash were checked.
cli.verify.by_replay: by re-running the spec, not by trusting its answers
verify.sweep.level.no_predicate: calibration: there is no predicate to certify
reducers.unknown: there is no standard reduction for a {type}: pass reduce=<callable> saying what one step smaller means, or one of sets / sequences / decrement / graphs / masks / hypotheses
reducers.bad: reduce must be a callable or a reducer name, not a {got}
orbits.unhashable: canonicalize must return something hashable, not a {got}: it is used as a dictionary key
verify.orbits.distinct: each orbit has its own representative
verify.orbits.representative: each representative belongs to its orbit
engine.sweep.spot_ok: {n} spot checks agreed with their representative
engine.sweep.spot_failed: the predicate is NOT invariant under the declared symmetry: {item} disagrees with its representative {rep}. Sweeping by orbit is unsound here -- drop --by-orbit
cli.orbits.assumed: --by-orbit evaluated one item per orbit. That the predicate is invariant under your symmetry is ASSUMED, not proved; {n} spot checks agreed.
doctor.what.pulp: opt, farkas (the exact LP behind both)

doctor.what.drat_trim: a second opinion on DRAT proofs

doctor.without.mpmath: python-flint covers everything mpmath does and more
doctor.without.nauty: the built-in Python engine, comfortable to n=8
doctor.without.cadical: the built-in CDCL: correct, and slow
doctor.without.kissat: the built-in CDCL: correct, and slow
doctor.without.drat_trim: the built-in Python DRUP/DRAT checker is enough
doctor.without.lean: export --lean still writes the file; nothing compiles it here
